properties.Notes: This probable camp was identified by Bryn Gethin. Partial geophysical survey has confirmed the extension of the western ditch south from where it can be traced on the ground, which establishes that this enclosure is earlier than the surrounding field system. Given it size and form, a Roman temporary camp seems to be the logical interpretation.

Pont Rhydgaled Roman marching camp lies towards the eastern edge of the Llechwedd Hirgoed ridge at 400m O.D. in the upper Wye valley 1.5Km northeast of Cae Gaer Roman fort (NPRN 92506). The camp measures 417m east-west by 311m north-south, enclosing 13 hectares. The camp survives as a vestigial earthwork partly cut by modern agricultural tracks; the NW and SE corners are also obscured by modern forestry plantations. A low earthwork of an inturned clavicula gate survives centrally in the west side, and one is visible offset in the north side; a damaged earthwork of an inturned clavicula can be seen centrally in the east side. The camp is defined by a single low rampart on all sides except the east, where the earthwork appears as a double line. This is an important addition to our understanding of the Roman campaigns west to Cardigan Bay.
properties.Source: Driver, T. , 2023 , Aerial archaeology in Wales during the 2022-23 droughts: major discoveries. Including recently catalogued additional discoveries from 2018 , Archaeology in Wales : 63 : 79-100

properties.Notes: Very heavily denuded Roman camp identified during lidar & aerial photographic analysis by Toby Driver. Camp is large, measuring 520m east-west x 385m north-south. Possesses characteristic ‘playing card’ shape of the camp, with rounded corners (surviving well at the SE angle), a ‘clavicula’ gateway on the west which is protected by a curving inturned bank, and also a possible annexe on the south east side.
